root_idea.summary: The root centers on bewilderment, perplexity, and being struck speechless; in a related development, an outrageous falsehood is one that overwhelms or bewilders its hearer.
root_idea.development: The intransitive verb denotes becoming confounded, while its transitive use denotes causing that state. بُهْتَانٌ extends the association to calumny or falsehood so shocking that it confounds the hearer.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I citation form بَهَتَ, covering the Quranic passive and active inflections.
Displayed as the nominal citation form بُهْتَانٌ.

senses.definition: To become confounded, perplexed, or astonished, unable to discern the right course.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic passive form, the subject is left bewildered or struck speechless; the usage describes a state resulting from an overwhelming argument or realization.

senses.definition: To cause someone to become confounded or bewildered, including by an unexpected onset.
senses.usage_conditions: The transitive construction presents the object as overwhelmed or unable to respond; suddenness may be supplied by the surrounding context rather than by the verb alone.

senses.definition: A calumny, slander, false accusation, or shocking lie.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic noun can denote a fabricated charge or falsehood so outrageous that it bewilders the hearer. In 60:12, it has been interpreted either as an allusion to adultery or more broadly as any reprehensible act carried out by hand or foot; the narrower interpretation is not required by the lexical meaning alone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be overcome in a dispute by an argument, allegation, or plea.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use describing the defeated party in disputation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To calumniate, slander, or falsely accuse someone; to forge a lie against them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a transitive use. It can include directly accusing someone of an act they did not commit, including a false accusation of adultery.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remove a stallion from a she-camel so that a stallion of more generous stock may cover her.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized breeding term used with the construction بَهَتَ الفَحْلَ عَنِ النَّاقَةِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To engage with another in mutual calumny, slander, or false accusation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or mutual Form III construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To confound or perplex another by what one fabricates against them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The confounding is produced through a forged charge or fabricated allegation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain well-known kind of stone.
A sidereal computation or calculation of the direct course of the stars in a day.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical term whose Arabic status is reported as doubtful by one authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an exclamatory idiom, an expression of appeal for help against calumny or of astonishment at it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction varies in vocalization according to whether it calls for aid or expresses wonder.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An intensive or habitual calumniator, slanderer, or false accuser; one who confounds a hearer by fabricated charges.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may also describe one who falsely accuses a woman of adultery, but that example does not limit its general application.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who causes another to become confounded, or who calumniates or falsely accuses another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participial noun from the transitive Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Confounded, perplexed, or amazed and unable to discern the right course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial description of the person affected by bewilderment.
A passive participial description of the person against whom a false charge has been made.

cautions: The Form I Quran group contains both the passive perfect بُهِتَ and the active imperfect تَبْهَتُ; the public headword is normalized to the classical citation form بَهَتَ, with the two Quranic constructions distinguished as separate senses.

The interpretation of بُهْتَانٍ in 60:12 varies between an allusion to adultery and a broader reference to reprehensible acts; the artifact preserves both as interpretive possibilities without making the narrower reading definitional.
Historical Quran citation notation in the lexical evidence is not converted directly into modern verse coordinates; the examples use the independently supplied QAC locations.
